sourcedFrom: FNS™ AUTOLOADING PISTOL OWNER'S MANUAL — 1608-FNS-OM 66237 (UNKNOWN — not printed in the document)
cleanIntro: A striker-fired polymer 9mm that field strips into four pieces: lock the slide back, turn the takedown lever down, release the striker, and run the slide off the front of the frame. FN's FNS book stops there and says so, and Deep Clean follows it only as far as it goes — the magazine down to its spring and follower, and the interchangeable backstrap.

steps.title: Read the slide: this book is for the FNS
steps.action: Before you start, read the inscriptions on the front left side of the slide. This guide follows FN's FNS book, written for pistols marked FNS-9 or FNS-9C and 9mm (and the .40 S&W FNS-40 and FNS-40C). If yours carries any other marking, or does not look like the pistol FN draws, stop and get the book for the pistol you have.
steps.prose: FN builds several striker-fired pistols that look alike on a bench — the FNS, the 509 and the 510 among them — and their takedown levers do not turn the same amount. FN's own words are that the instructions differ by pistol type, which is why the slide marking, not the outline, decides which book you follow. The FNS-9 Longslide and the FNS-9 Compact are both FNS pistols and are covered by this same book.
steps.quote: Warnings and instructions are different for each type of pistol.
steps.cite: FNS™ AUTOLOADING PISTOL OWNER'S MANUAL — 1608-FNS-OM 66237 — Foreword block, p.2

steps.title: Muzzle safe, and the manual safety on if yours has one
steps.action: Point the muzzle in a safe direction and keep your fingers off the trigger. Look at the rear of the frame above the grip: if there is a serrated lever on each side, raise it until it clicks and the red dot is covered. If there is no lever, your FNS has only the trigger safety and there is nothing to set.
steps.prose: FN sells the FNS both ways and the same book covers both, so the manual cannot tell you which one is in your hand. Some FNS models carry an ambidextrous manual safety; the others rely on the articulated trigger and internal safeties. Do not judge the lever by the red dot alone — FN warns the colour can be worn away by time and cleaning agents.
steps.quote: 1. If your pistol is so equipped, place the manual safety lever in the on safe position as described in Section 8.1.
steps.cite: FNS™ AUTOLOADING PISTOL OWNER'S MANUAL — 1608-FNS-OM 66237 — §16.1 Unloading the pistol, step 1, p.28

steps.title: Magazine out, and pull it if it sticks
steps.action: Press the ambidextrous magazine release and take the magazine out. If it does not drop free, keep the release pressed and pull on the magazine's bottom plate.
steps.prose: The magazine always comes out before the slide moves: with it still seated, working the slide just loads a fresh round into the chamber. The release works from either side. Put the magazine down away from the bench where the pistol will be stripped — FN also notes the slide cannot go back onto the frame with a magazine in the well, so it has to be out for the whole job.
steps.quote: 2. Press the ambidextrous magazine release and remove the magazine. If the magazine does not drop out of the pistol, pull on the bottom plate while pressing the ambidextrous magazine release.
steps.cite: FNS™ AUTOLOADING PISTOL OWNER'S MANUAL — 1608-FNS-OM 66237 — §16.1 Unloading the pistol, step 2, p.28

steps.title: Rack any round out of the chamber
steps.action: With the magazine out, pull the slide fully back to eject any cartridge from the chamber, then press the ambidextrous slide stop up to lock the slide open.
steps.prose: One full, firm stroke: a short pull can draw a round part way and let it fall back in. The slide stop sits on both sides of the frame above the trigger, so either thumb can hold it up while the other hand eases the slide onto it. With the slide locked open, the chamber is in view for the next check.
steps.quote: 3. If the slide is closed, remove the magazine and then pull back on the slide and eject any cartridge in the chamber.
steps.cite: FNS™ AUTOLOADING PISTOL OWNER'S MANUAL — 1608-FNS-OM 66237 — §16.1 Unloading the pistol, step 3, p.28

steps.title: Look into the chamber and the magazine well
steps.action: With the slide open, look through the ejection port into the chamber and down into the magazine well. Both must be empty before you go on.
steps.prose: The FNS has a loaded chamber indicator on the right side of the slide behind the ejection port, which stands out and shows red when a round is chambered. It is a useful tell that a round is there and a poor way to decide one is not, because the red can wear off. This is the look the whole strip rests on, because a later step presses the trigger.
steps.quote: 1. Completely unload the pistol as described in Section 16.1. and remove the magazine. Inspect the chamber and the magazine well to verify that the pistol is completely unloaded.
steps.cite: FNS™ AUTOLOADING PISTOL OWNER'S MANUAL — 1608-FNS-OM 66237 — §17.1 Disassembling the pistol, step 1, p.30

steps.title: Slide locked to the rear
steps.action: Pull the slide fully to the rear and press the ambidextrous slide stop up so the slide stays locked open.
steps.prose: The takedown lever will not turn with the slide forward, so this is the position the next step needs. If the slide has crept off the stop while you checked the chamber, run it back again rather than forcing the lever. Keep the muzzle pointed somewhere safe from here to the end of the strip.
steps.quote: 2. Pull the slide fully rearward and lock it into its rear position by pressing the ambidextrous slide stop upward.
steps.cite: FNS™ AUTOLOADING PISTOL OWNER'S MANUAL — 1608-FNS-OM 66237 — §17.1 Disassembling the pistol, step 2, p.30

steps.title: Takedown lever a quarter turn down
steps.action: Rotate the takedown lever, on the left side of the frame above the trigger, 90 degrees clockwise so it points down.
steps.prose: On the FNS the lever travels a right angle and stops — 90 degrees, where some of FN's later pistols want more. If it resists, check the slide is still locked fully back before applying more force; leaning on a lever against a closed slide is how its edges get marked.
steps.cite: FNS™ AUTOLOADING PISTOL OWNER'S MANUAL — 1608-FNS-OM 66237 — §17.1 Disassembling the pistol, step 3, p.30

steps.title: Let the slide forward under your hand
steps.action: Hold the slide firmly with one hand and release it, either by pressing the slide stop down or by pushing the slide slightly to the rear. Let it come forward under control, not at speed.
steps.prose: The recoil spring is still driving the slide, and with the takedown lever down nothing but your hand stops it running forward. A slide allowed to slam here can come further than you want and catch the striker again. Keep the grip until the slide has stopped moving.
steps.quote: Be sure to have a firm grip on the slide as it is under pressure of the recoil spring.
steps.cite: FNS™ AUTOLOADING PISTOL OWNER'S MANUAL — 1608-FNS-OM 66237 — §17.1 Disassembling the pistol, step 4, p.31

steps.title: Check it is empty again, then press the trigger
steps.action: Pull the slide back once more and look into the chamber and the magazine well. Then, with the rear of the slide held level with the rear of the frame and the muzzle in a safe direction, squeeze the trigger to release the striker. The slide moves forward about a quarter inch when it releases properly.
steps.prose: FN prints this as a warning in capitals and asks for the second look on purpose: this is the one step where the trigger is pressed. Keeping the slide and frame rear faces in line is what lets the striker drop cleanly. If the slide is pushed too far forward it does not release, and you will feel the striker still cocked.
steps.quote: 5. While keeping the rear of the slide and the rear of the frame in alignment, point the muzzle in a safe direction and squeeze the trigger to release the striker.
steps.cite: FNS™ AUTOLOADING PISTOL OWNER'S MANUAL — 1608-FNS-OM 66237 — §17.1 Disassembling the pistol, step 5, p.31
steps.warn: THE PISTOL MUST BE COMPLETELY UNLOADED TO PERFORM STEP 5. AGAIN, ENSURE THE PISTOL IS COMPLETELY UNLOADED BY PULLING BACK THE SLIDE AND INSPECTING THE CHAMBER AND THE MAGAZINE WELL.

steps.title: Slide forward and off the frame
steps.action: Pull the slide firmly forward and away from the frame. It comes off as one assembly with the barrel and recoil spring inside. If the striker has recocked, go back and release it again before pulling.
steps.prose: FN says plainly that this can take extra force, so a firm pull is normal and is not a sign something is wrong. What is wrong is fighting a recocked striker — the slide will not clear the frame while the striker is still caught, and pulling harder only wears the rails. Support the slide as it comes free so it does not drop.
steps.quote: 6. After releasing the striker you can remove the slide by forcefully pulling the slide forward away from the frame.
steps.cite: FNS™ AUTOLOADING PISTOL OWNER'S MANUAL — 1608-FNS-OM 66237 — §17.1 Disassembling the pistol, step 6, p.31

steps.title: Recoil spring out: compress, free the rear, lift
steps.action: Turn the slide upside down. Compress the recoil spring gently, free its rear end from the barrel lug, and lift the spring up and out of the slide.
steps.prose: The spring's rear end sits on the barrel lug under load, so it has to be compressed a little before it will come off — lifting it straight up without that drags it across the lug. Gentle is FN's word, and the spring is close to your face here, so the eye protection FN calls for is worth having on. Set it down whole.
steps.quote: 8. While gently compressing the recoil spring, release the rear from the barrel lug and then lift the spring up and out of the slide (Figure 17).
steps.cite: FNS™ AUTOLOADING PISTOL OWNER'S MANUAL — 1608-FNS-OM 66237 — §17.1 Disassembling the pistol, step 8, p.31

steps.title: Barrel up and out by its lug
steps.action: Take hold of the barrel by its lug and lift it up and out of the slide.
steps.prose: The lug is the solid block under the chamber, and it is the handle FN tells you to use. Gripping it there keeps your fingers off the bore and the muzzle crown, which FN asks you to protect. That finishes the strip.
steps.quote: 9. Grip the barrel by its lug and then lift it up and out of the slide (Figure 18).
steps.cite: FNS™ AUTOLOADING PISTOL OWNER'S MANUAL — 1608-FNS-OM 66237 — §17.1 Disassembling the pistol, step 9, p.32

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: Four pieces on the bench: frame, slide, barrel and recoil spring. FN says that is enough for a thorough cleaning and that the pistol is not to be taken apart beyond this point.
steps.prose: Everything the cleaning section names is now in reach: the bore from the chamber end, the slide, chamber and extractor, the frame's magazine housing and the lubrication points on both rails. FN reserves any further disassembly to an authorised armorer or the FN Product Service Center. Deep Clean covers the two things the book does take further — the magazine and the backstrap.
steps.quote: This level of disassembly (Figure 19) is sufficient to perform a thorough cleaning.
steps.cite: FNS™ AUTOLOADING PISTOL OWNER'S MANUAL — 1608-FNS-OM 66237 — §17.1 Disassembling the pistol, closing note, p.32
steps.warn: Do not disassemble the pistol beyond this point.

deepSteps.title: Magazine: press the retainer through the floorplate
deepSteps.action: With the magazine out of the pistol and empty, press on the part of the magazine retainer that shows through the hole in the floorplate, using a small screwdriver or similar tool. Hold the retainer down and slide the floorplate a little forward.
deepSteps.prose: FN treats this as part of normal maintenance, not an armorer's job, and it takes seconds. The retainer is what holds the spring in, so it pushes back against your tool. Cover the floorplate with your thumb as it starts to move, as FN's figure shows, so the spring cannot launch it.
deepSteps.quote: 2. Using a tool such as a small screwdriver, press on the protruding part of the magazine retainer through the hole in the floorplate (Figure 22, page 37).
deepSteps.cite: FNS™ AUTOLOADING PISTOL OWNER'S MANUAL — 1608-FNS-OM 66237 — §17.5 Disassembling the magazine, step 2, p.36
deepSteps.warn: WEAR EYE PROTECTION WHEN DISASSEMBLING, ASSEMBLING AND CLEANING YOUR PISTOL AND MAGAZINE TO PREVENT SPRING-LOADED PARTS, SOLVENTS OR OTHER AGENTS FROM CONTACTING YOUR EYES, RESULTING IN INJURY.

deepSteps.title: Floorplate off, spring let out slowly
deepSteps.action: Keep holding the retainer in place, slide the floorplate off the magazine body, then let the magazine spring out carefully — it is under pressure.
deepSteps.prose: A 17-round spring has a lot of stored length, and the retainer is the only thing between it and the room. Let it rise under your thumb rather than lifting your hand away. Point the open end of the magazine away from your face while you do it.
deepSteps.quote: 3. While holding the retainer (which is subjected to the force of the magazine spring) in position, slide the floor plate off the magazine body and then carefully release the magazine spring which is under pressure.
deepSteps.cite: FNS™ AUTOLOADING PISTOL OWNER'S MANUAL — 1608-FNS-OM 66237 — §17.5 Disassembling the magazine, step 3, p.36

deepSteps.title: Spring, follower and retainer out — and stop there
deepSteps.action: Take the magazine spring out of the body together with the follower and the retainer. That is as far as the magazine comes apart.
deepSteps.prose: FN says this is enough for a thorough magazine cleaning and sends anything further to an authorised armorer or the FN Product Service Center. Note which way the follower sits on the spring before you separate anything, because FN's reassembly asks for it to go back the right way round.
deepSteps.quote: 4. Remove the magazine spring together with the follower and retainer.
deepSteps.cite: FNS™ AUTOLOADING PISTOL OWNER'S MANUAL — 1608-FNS-OM 66237 — §17.5 Disassembling the magazine, step 4, p.37

deepSteps.title: Magazine clean, and dry inside
deepSteps.action: Clean all the magazine parts with a soft cloth or rag. Wipe a light coat of lubricant over the outside metal surfaces with a moistened cloth, wipe off the excess, and make sure the inside of the magazine is dry.
deepSteps.prose: Oil inside a magazine body collects the grit that makes a follower drag and a round nose-dive. The outside gets a light film against rust and the inside stays dry. A dirty magazine is the first thing FN's troubleshooting matrix suggests for a failure to feed.
deepSteps.quote: Ensure that the inside of the magazine is dry.
deepSteps.cite: FNS™ AUTOLOADING PISTOL OWNER'S MANUAL — 1608-FNS-OM 66237 — §17.6 Cleaning and lubrication of the magazine, step 3, p.37

deepSteps.title: Backstrap off — FNS-9 and FNS-9 Longslide
deepSteps.action: On the full-size FNS-9 or the Longslide, put a 1/16" punch or other small tool into the hole in the backstrap and push gently inward to release the backstrap retainer. Keep light pressure on the punch and slide the backstrap down off the grip.
deepSteps.prose: This gives you the grip surface underneath, where sweat and lint collect on a carried pistol. A replacement backstrap goes on by sliding it up the rail until it snaps into place. Make sure the pistol is unloaded before you start; FN puts that warning at the head of the section.
deepSteps.quote: 1. Insert a 1/16" punch or other small instrument into the hole in the backstrap and gently push inward to release the backstrap retainer (Figure 26, page 40).
deepSteps.cite: FNS™ AUTOLOADING PISTOL OWNER'S MANUAL — 1608-FNS-OM 66237 — §19.1 Interchangeable backstraps, step 1, p.39

deepSteps.title: Backstrap off — FNS-9 Compact
deepSteps.action: On the Compact, the backstrap is held by a pin rather than a retainer. Drive the backstrap retaining pin out with a 1/16" punch, then slide the backstrap down off the grip. It goes back by sliding it up the rail and refitting the pin.
deepSteps.prose: FN gives the Compact its own procedure because its backstrap is pinned, and pushing at the hole as you would on the full-size pistol will not release it. Use a punch of the size FN names so the pin is not damaged, and keep it somewhere safe while the backstrap is off.
deepSteps.quote: 1. Remove the backstrap retaining pin using a 1/16" punch.
deepSteps.cite: FNS™ AUTOLOADING PISTOL OWNER'S MANUAL — 1608-FNS-OM 66237 — §19.1 Interchangeable backstraps, FNS Compact, step 1, p.40

deepSteps.title: No further: the rest is FN's or a gunsmith's
deepSteps.action: Do not take the pistol apart any further than the field strip, the magazine and the backstrap. If more service or cleaning is needed, take it to a qualified gunsmith or send it to FN's service facility.
deepSteps.prose: FN calls the FNS a specialised, finely fitted mechanism and warns that opening the inner assemblies can damage it permanently. FN also recommends an inspection by a qualified gunsmith or the FN Product Service Center every 2,000 rounds and/or once a year, because wear and corrosion do not always show from the outside.
deepSteps.quote: NEVER ATTEMPT TO TAKE YOUR PISTOL APART FURTHER THAN EXPLAINED IN THIS OWNER’S MANUAL.
deepSteps.cite: FNS™ AUTOLOADING PISTOL OWNER'S MANUAL — 1608-FNS-OM 66237 — §18 Taking care of the pistol, notice, p.38

cleaning.name: BARREL & BORE
tasks: Brush or spray solvent into the barrel and leave it a few minutes to penetrate
Rod, jag and patches of the right size, back and forth until the patches come out clean
Clean from the chamber end only — FN warns a scratched or damaged muzzle can affect accuracy
Finish with a patch moistened with storage lubricant to protect the bore until next use
Wipe the bore dry before the next time you shoot

cleaning.name: SLIDE, CHAMBER & FRAME
tasks: Brush and solvent on the slide, chamber, extractor and anywhere powder and primer residue collects
Soft cloth (with solvent if needed) to take dirt out of the frame's magazine housing
Clean every part of the pistol thoroughly
Check the parts for wear or damage; if in doubt about one, ask your dealer or armorer before reassembling

cleaning.name: LUBRICATION
tasks: Light film of gun oil from a moistened cloth on all external metal surfaces; the polymer grip and frame need none
One drop of lubricant at each point in FN's diagrams: the frame rails, disconnector, disconnector cam, cam spring and unlock block
One drop on the slide rails, barrel contact surfaces, cartridge guide surface, disconnector cam recess, barrel lock-up and unlock surfaces
Do not use too much lubricant — FN warns it can interfere with function
Never soak the pistol in hydrocarbons, ammonia, trichloroethylene or Teflon-based lubricants
Wipe the outside clean of dirt, fingerprints and excess lubricant when it is back together

cleaning.name: HOW OFTEN
tasks: Clean and lubricate after every use, or every 500 rounds in intensive shooting
Sooner in bad weather or with excessively dirty ammunition
Inspection by a qualified gunsmith or FN every 2,000 rounds and/or once a year

reassembly: Barrel into the slide, with the muzzle facing the right way.
Recoil spring in: its front end seated in its position in the slide, its rear end fitted onto the barrel lug.
Magazine out of the well — the slide will not go onto the frame with a magazine inserted. Line the rail grooves in the slide up with the guides on the frame and put the slide on.
Pull the slide fully to the rear and lift the ambidextrous slide stop to lock it back.
Rotate the takedown lever 90 degrees counterclockwise.
Pull the slide rearward to release the slide stop and ease the slide forward.
If your FNS has a manual safety, put it in the on safe position straight away.

Magazine, if you stripped it: follower fitted onto the spring the right way round, spring and follower into the body, then hold the spring down with the retainer and slide the floorplate on until it locks into position.
fncheck: With no ammunition anywhere near the bench — FN says never to test the mechanical function with live ammunition: the slide should run forward under its spring and lock open when you pull it back and press the slide stop up; pressing the slide stop down or pulling the slide back should release it. An empty magazine should drop from the well when the ambidextrous release is pressed, and click home when inserted. On a pistol with a manual safety, the lever should click up to on safe with the red dot fully covered and down to off safe with the dot showing. If the pistol later sounds or feels different when firing, FN's instruction is to stop, point it in a safe direction, unload it, and go to the troubleshooting guide.
